title: Adapter & codec-based contract for streaming + tool invocations (multi-SDK migration)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a language-agnostic adapter + codec layer that standardizes streamed tokens, structured output events, and tool/function-calling contracts across TypeScript/Python/Go SDKs and provides a migration path for existing integrations.

Scope:
- Define a compact event codec (JSON-line + typed envelope) used by runtime to emit: partial tokens, structured schema deltas, tool invocation requests/responses, and terminal events.
- Implement adapters in TS/Py/Go that translate native SDK streaming callbacks into the codec and expose typed helpers for decoding structured outputs and tool responses.
- Provide migration shims that accept legacy streaming shapes and map them to the new envelope for backwards compatibility.
- Add example snippets and a migration guide for customers and internal samples (chat, function-calling, and reranker flows).

Non-goals:
- Not changing wire-level transport (still HTTP/1.1 streaming & SSE for hosted).
- Not altering model-side schema semantics (we assume schema metadata from model manifest).
tasks: Draft codec envelope spec + sequence semantics (version v1) - RFC
Implement TypeScript adapter with typed decoder + convenience builders
Implement Python adapter with sync/async decoders and dataclass helpers
Implement Go adapter with streaming tokenizer and minimal allocator paths
Add migration shim that accepts old 'delta' streaming shapes and maps events to new envelope
Write end-to-end tests (unit + integration against staging runtime) for chunk reassembly and tool call roundtrip
Author migration guide and multi-language examples (chat, tool-call, structured-schema)
Open cross-repo PRs: sdk-js, sdk-py, sdk-go; coordinate reviews
acceptance_criteria: Codec RFC published and approved by runtime + SDK leads
TS/Py/Go adapters implemented with identical event semantics documented
Backward-compat shim passes existing SDK e2e test suite
Examples + migration guide added to /docs/sdk/migration/codec-v1.md and included in console quickstarts
Performance: streaming latency overhead < 1.5ms/sample added by adapter on our staging GPU profile
PRs merged for sdk-js, sdk-py, sdk-go and release branch cut for sdk-2026.04
notes: Decision: use a newline-delimited JSON envelope with a top-level 't' (type) and 'id' fields to make reparsing while streaming deterministic.
Trade-off: slightly larger payload per event vs easier language decoding and forwards-compat. Chosen to favor developer ergonomics.
Compatibility: migration shim will accept legacy 'delta' + 'tool_call' events and synthesize envelope.type values 'token','schema','tool_request','tool_response','done'.
Security: adapters must surface raw event for customers with encryption-at-rest so KMS integrations are unaffected. See security checklist in RFC.

Edge-case: models that emit interleaved JSON and plain text (bad schema) will generate 'schema_error' events rather than failing the stream. SDK will surface both the error and the raw chunk for diagnostics.

examples: TS snippet: client.stream({onEvent: decodeEnvelope, onError: (e)=>console.error(e)}); // decodeEnvelope returns typed union for token/schema/tool
Py snippet: with client.stream() as s: for raw in s: evt = CodecV1.decode(raw); handle(evt)
Go snippet: dec := codec.NewDecoder(r); for dec.Next() { evt := dec.Event(); switch evt.Type { case "token": ... } }
Migration example: shim maps legacy 'delta'->'token' and merges fragmented 'tool_response' chunks into a single 'tool_response' event before decoding.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: language SDKs interpret streaming boundaries differently, causing partial JSON parse failures. Mitigation: envelope includes 'len' and a checksum field to allow resync and diagnostic logging.
Risk: customers with strict binary transports may not accept newline-delimited JSON. Mitigation: provide a binary protobuf variant behind a feature flag for enterprise/private deployments.

Risk: breaking change in downstream customers if migration is forced. Mitigation: ship adapters behind a minor version and default to legacy shape with opt-in codec-v1; provide autoconvert CLI to help large customers.
outstanding_questions: Should the envelope include a top-level deterministic timestamp from runtime or rely on client-side arrival times? (runtime prefers server timestamp)
Do we add an explicit 'schema_version' field to every structured output event or only the first event? (leaning toward per-event for patchability)
What verbosity should the debug 'raw_chunk' mode include for PIIs? Need security review before enabling by default.
